RECAP.t: Stocks bounced in early trading after Tuesday's inflation scare: the S&P 500 rose about 1% and the Nasdaq 1.6%, led by a 17% jump in CoreWeave after strong earnings. Bond markets are closed for Veterans Day, and traders now fully expect a Fed rate hike in December.

CAL: Wholesale inflation for October. After Tuesday's hot CPI, another strong number would add to rate-hike bets.
How much Americans spent in October, a key read on the consumer before the holidays. Home Depot and Nvidia also report.
Notes from the Oct 27–28 Fed meeting, which show how many officials want more rate hikes.
The second estimate of Q3 growth plus the Fed's favorite inflation gauge, the day before Thanksgiving.

NEWS.h: AI stocks bounce back: the Nasdaq jumps about 1.6% as CoreWeave soars 17%
NEWS.w: In early trading the S&P 500 rose about 1%, the Nasdaq 1.6% and the Dow 0.2%. CoreWeave jumped about 17% after Q3 revenue rose 168% to $3.7 billion and it raised its full-year revenue outlook to $13–13.3 billion. Nvidia gained about 3% after a two-day drop that erased more than $430 billion in value.
NEWS.m: After a big sell-off, strong numbers from one AI company can lift the whole group. But CoreWeave still lost $709 million in the quarter, so investors are paying for growth, not profit.
NEWS.a: Good interview point: revenue growth and profitability are different things. A company can grow 168% and still lose money, so look at margins and cash flow, not only the top line.

NEWS.h: Markets now fully expect a December Fed rate hike, and Goldman adds one in March
NEWS.w: After Tuesday's hot inflation report, traders fully price a 0.25% Fed rate hike in December and about 10% odds of a bigger 0.5% move. Goldman Sachs added a March hike to its forecast, and markets now see about three more hikes by mid-2027. The 2-year Treasury yield had its biggest jump since April 2025.
NEWS.m: Higher rates make borrowing more expensive for companies and buyers, which can slow down deals and LBOs and push stock valuations lower.
NEWS.a: If asked about the market: higher rates raise the discount rate in a DCF, which lowers present values, and they make LBO debt more expensive, which lowers the price a PE firm can pay.

NEWS.h: Anthropic's IPO reportedly seeks up to $90 billion at about a $1.4 trillion valuation
NEWS.w: Anthropic and existing shareholders are reportedly seeking up to $90.4 billion through the IPO and a related private placement, at a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion, and the deal has reportedly drawn several times more orders than shares available.
NEWS.m: An IPO this big would pay record fees to the banks running it and is a big test of investor appetite for AI right after a sharp sell-off.
NEWS.a: Know the IPO basics: banks underwrite the offering, build an order book from investors and help set the price. Being 'oversubscribed' means demand is higher than the shares on offer.

NEWS.h: A hotter inflation report knocks stocks lower and pushes the 10-year yield back above 5%
NEWS.w: October consumer prices rose 0.4%, and core prices (without food and energy) rose 0.3% for a third straight month. The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Nasdaq 0.7% and the Dow 0.3%, while the 10-year Treasury yield climbed back above 5% during the day.
NEWS.m: Sticky inflation makes a Fed rate hike in December more likely. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he leans toward a quarter-point hike, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said two more hikes will be needed.
NEWS.a: Interviewers often ask how rates affect valuation. Higher rates raise the discount rate in a DCF, which lowers the present value of future cash flows, and long-duration growth stocks like tech feel it most.

NEWS.h: Nvidia drops 5.5% as its board investigates CEO Jensen Huang
NEWS.w: Nvidia fell 5.47% and its market value briefly slipped under $4 trillion, after falling more than 4% the day before. Its independent directors hired a law firm to look into a weekend email from Huang and a report about a possible foreign spying attempt.
NEWS.m: Nvidia is so large that its moves drag the whole market down, and the stock is down about 30% in five weeks. Key-person risk matters even for the biggest companies.
NEWS.a: A good interview point: governance and key-person risk can hit valuation even when the business is strong. Investors may demand a higher discount rate until the uncertainty clears.

NEWS.h: Stocks jump 2.4% as oil falls and fear eases
NEWS.w: The S&P 500 rose 2.4% to 7,549.94, the Nasdaq gained 2.7% and the Dow added 1,104 points to 52,389.75. All 11 sectors rose, oil fell about 1% and the VIX fear gauge dropped 22%.
NEWS.m: Big one-day rallies often come when fear has built up and then eases. Lower oil prices help by cooling inflation worries.
NEWS.a: If asked what the VIX is, say it measures how much movement options traders expect over the next 30 days. A falling VIX means investors are calmer.

NEWS.h: KKR posts record profit and plans to return over $40 billion to its investors
NEWS.w: KKR's adjusted net income rose 29% to $1.6 billion, or $1.78 a share, above the $1.59 analysts expected. It plans to return more than $40 billion to clients in 2026, over 50% above its old record.
NEWS.m: Returning cash to investors (exits) has been the weak spot for private equity. Big distributions help firms raise their next funds.
NEWS.a: In a PE interview, connect exits to fundraising: investors (LPs) need cash back before they commit to new funds, so a strong exit year makes future fundraising easier.

NEWS.h: NRG sells six gas power plants to LS Power for $4 billion
NEWS.w: NRG Energy agreed to sell six gas-fired plants, about 4.9 gigawatts of power, to LS Power for $4 billion in cash, about 8 times estimated 2027 adjusted EBITDA. NRG shares rose about 9.5% after it also beat earnings estimates.
NEWS.m: NRG will use the cash for $2 billion of debt paydown and $1 billion of buybacks. Power plants are in demand as AI data centers need more electricity.
NEWS.a: This is a clean example of a divestiture: a seller trims assets to cut debt and return cash. Interviewers like it when you tie the price (8x EBITDA) to how the seller uses the proceeds.

NEWS.h: Brad Jacobs leads a $1 billion investment into tiny CKX Lands, and its stock jumps 85%
NEWS.w: CKX Lands announced a $1 billion cash investment led by Brad Jacobs, with $900 million from Jacobs Private Equity II. Jacobs will become chairman and CEO, and the company plans to rename itself; the target industry hasn't been disclosed.
NEWS.m: Jacobs has built big companies through acquisitions before, including QXO, so investors bet he'll do it again here.
NEWS.a: This is a roll-up setup: a public shell plus fresh capital to buy many smaller companies. In interviews, say roll-ups work when buying smaller firms at lower multiples creates value once combined.

NEWS.h: Employers add 165,000 jobs in October, far above forecasts
NEWS.w: The economy added 165,000 jobs versus about 65,000 expected, and unemployment fell to 4.1%. Wages rose 3.1% from a year earlier, and the prior two months were revised up by 84,000 jobs.
NEWS.m: A strong job market plus faster wage growth raises the odds of a Fed rate hike. Markets put the chance of a December hike at about 77%.
NEWS.a: If asked how jobs data moves markets, explain the chain: strong jobs and wages mean more inflation pressure, which means higher rates, which lowers stock valuations and raises bond yields.

NEWS.h: Democrats projected to win the House and Senate, and stock futures slip
NEWS.w: TV networks projected that Democrats will take control of both chambers of Congress after Tuesday's midterm elections. Overnight, S&P 500 futures fell about 0.5% and Nasdaq futures about 0.9%, while the dollar weakened.
NEWS.m: A split government, with a Republican president and a Democratic Congress, usually means fewer big new laws. Analysts said a narrow Democratic win was largely expected, and that tech fell more on worries about tighter rules for Big Tech and AI. UBS still expects the push to loosen bank rules to continue.
NEWS.a: Interviewers like to ask how politics moves markets. A clean answer: markets hate uncertainty more than either party, so once results are clear, deal and IPO activity can pick up. Name one sector exposed to policy, like tech regulation or bank capital rules.

NEWS.h: AMD's sales jump 45% and it forecasts about $17 billion next quarter
NEWS.w: AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45% from a year earlier, with record data center sales of $8.5 billion, nearly double last year. It guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17 billion, and the stock jumped in after-hours trading.
NEWS.m: After weeks of doubts about AI spending, a chipmaker forecasting 66% growth next quarter is a sign the AI build-out is still running hot. It helped lift Asian tech stocks overnight.
NEWS.a: Show you know guidance often matters more than the quarter itself. The stock trades on what investors expect next, so a big forecast above estimates can move the price more than a small beat on past results.

NEWS.h: Chips lift the Nasdaq 0.8% while Apple drags the Dow lower
NEWS.w: The Nasdaq rose 0.83% to 25,372 and the S&P 500 gained 0.36% to 7,569 as Nvidia, Broadcom and other chip stocks bounced. The Dow fell 0.38% to 51,787 as Apple slid 1.9% on a weaker profit-margin forecast tied to rising memory chip costs.
NEWS.m: The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 4.95%, close to 5%, which makes stocks look pricier next to safe bonds. Tech was the best of the S&P 500's 11 sectors, up 1.31%.
NEWS.a: Know why one stock can move the Dow so much: the Dow is price-weighted, so a high-priced stock like Apple counts more than a cheaper one, no matter how big each company is. The S&P 500 is weighted by market value instead.

NEWS.h: The Anthropic IPO could be the "swing vote" for big banks this quarter
NEWS.w: Anthropic's stock market debut could come as soon as Nov. 16, and all five of the largest U.S. banks are working on it. Evercore estimates the fees could add about 0.8% to the banks' fourth-quarter profits, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Citi gaining the most.
NEWS.m: Bank stocks need a boost: global investment banking activity fell 25% from a year earlier in October, as rising rates slowed deals and trading. At a Hong Kong summit, Goldman's David Solomon said good companies can still raise plenty of money, and Morgan Stanley's Ted Pick called AI investment the "second inning of a nine-inning game."
NEWS.a: Be ready to explain how banks make money on an IPO: they underwrite the deal, buying the shares and reselling them to investors, and keep a fee called the gross spread. Bigger IPOs mean bigger fees, which is why one deal can move a quarter.

NEWS.h: Apollo posts a $1.1 billion loss on paper, but its core fee business grows 23%
NEWS.w: Private markets giant Apollo reported a third-quarter GAAP net loss of $1.1 billion, mostly from mark-to-market losses at its retirement business as interest rates rose. Its fee-related earnings, the steady management fees, rose 23% to $802 million, and assets reached $1.07 trillion.
NEWS.m: Apollo's stock fell about 4.9% to $113.56. Investors watch fee earnings most because they recur, but the loss shows how higher rates hit firms that own big insurance companies, like Apollo's Athene.
NEWS.a: Great example for the question "why do bond values fall when rates rise?" Older bonds pay less than new ones, so their prices drop. Also know the difference between GAAP net income and fee-related earnings at an asset manager.

NEWS_QUIZ: CoreWeave's revenue rose 168% last quarter, but it still lost $709 million. What does that show?
A company can grow fast and still lose money
Revenue is the top line. Costs can still be larger than sales, so you need to check margins and cash flow too.
Why do higher interest rates usually hurt LBOs?
They make the target company bigger
They make the debt used to buy the company more expensive
LBOs are paid for mostly with debt. Higher rates raise interest costs, so a PE firm can borrow less and pay less.
What does it mean when an IPO is 'oversubscribed'?
Fewer investors want shares than are offered
Investors want more shares than are on offer
The bank bought all the shares itself
Oversubscribed means demand is bigger than supply, which can let the company price the IPO higher.

DEALS.target: Six NRG Energy gas power plants
DEALS.what: NRG Energy agreed to sell six gas-fired power plants to LS Power for $4 billion in cash. The deal is expected to close in the second quarter of 2027 after regulatory approvals.
DEALS.why: NRG wants to cut debt and return cash to shareholders, while LS Power is betting on rising power demand from AI data centers. NRG plans $2 billion of debt paydown and $1 billion of buybacks.
DEALS.say: "At about 8x 2027 EBITDA, NRG is turning plants into cash it can use to pay down $2 billion of debt and buy back stock, which is a classic way to unlock value through a divestiture."
q: NRG sold six gas plants to LS Power for $4 billion. What is this type of deal called from NRG's side?
A leveraged recapitalization
A divestiture of assets
A reverse merger
A spin-off to shareholders
Selling a group of assets to another company for cash is a divestiture. A spin-off would hand the assets to NRG's own shareholders instead.
LS Power paid about 8x estimated 2027 adjusted EBITDA for NRG's plants. Roughly what EBITDA does that imply for those plants?
About $320 million
About $800 million
About $500 million
About $1.2 billion
$4 billion divided by 8 is $500 million of expected yearly EBITDA.

DEALS.what: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum, a maker of lasers and optical parts for AI data centers, in an all-stock deal valued at about $115 billion, or about $1,132 per Lumentum share at Oct 28 prices. Marvell owners would hold about 67% of the combined company and Lumentum owners about 33%, with closing expected in the first half of 2028.
DEALS.why: Marvell makes chips that move data, and it wants more optical technology and factory capacity as AI data centers shift from copper to light. The companies expect more than $1 billion of yearly cost savings and say the deal should add to Marvell's adjusted EPS in the first year after closing.
DEALS.say: "Because Marvell is paying a fixed 4.5 shares, the $115 billion headline moves with its stock, so Lumentum's owners take on Marvell's share price risk until closing in 2028."
q: Marvell is paying a fixed 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share. If Marvell's stock falls before closing, what happens to Lumentum owners' payout?
It stays locked at the $1,132 headline price
It rises because Marvell issues extra shares
Its value falls because the 4.5 ratio is fixed
It converts into cash at the Oct 28 stock price
With a fixed exchange ratio, the share count stays the same, so the dollar value moves up and down with the buyer's stock.
Marvell must pay Lumentum $3.2 billion if the merger ends over certain regulatory problems. Why would Lumentum ask for this fee?
It pays Lumentum for failed-review risk
It lets Marvell skip the U.S. antitrust review
It raises the exchange ratio when deals close
It funds the $1 billion of planned cost savings
A reverse termination fee protects the target, which can lose years and business momentum if regulators block the merger.

DEALS.buyer: Blackstone and four Canadian pension investors
DEALS.target: 49.9% of a Mitsubishi LNG Canada unit
terms: Unit holds Mitsubishi's 15% of LNG Canada
Mitsubishi keeps its full LNG supply
DEALS.what: Blackstone, CPP Investments, OMERS, IMCO and PSP Investments agreed to pay US$3.1 billion for 49.9% of a Mitsubishi subsidiary. The subsidiary holds Mitsubishi's 15% interest in LNG Canada, the country's first liquefied natural gas export plant.
DEALS.why: Mitsubishi raises cash from a finished, long-life project while keeping control and its full share of the plant's gas. The investors get a stake in energy infrastructure, which pension funds like for steady, long-term income.
DEALS.say: "It's a minority stake sale: Mitsubishi gets $3.1 billion of cash and keeps control, and the price implies about $6.2 billion for the whole unit."
q: A Blackstone-led group is buying a 49.9% non-controlling stake in a Mitsubishi unit that holds part of LNG Canada. What does non-controlling mean here?
Blackstone's group can force a sale of the unit
Mitsubishi keeps majority ownership of the unit
Mitsubishi must buy the stake back within a year
The Canadian government must run the LNG plant
Holding under 50% means the investors own a big piece, but Mitsubishi keeps the majority and with it control.
Blackstone's group is paying $3.1 billion for 49.9% of a Mitsubishi LNG Canada unit. About what value does that imply for all of the unit?
$1.5 billion
$3.1 billion
$4.6 billion
$6.2 billion
Divide the price by the stake: $3.1 billion ÷ 0.499 ≈ $6.2 billion for 100% of the unit.

DEALS.what: Kansas City-based UMB Financial agreed to buy El Dorado Savings Bank, a California bank with about $2.4 billion of assets, for about $506 million in cash and stock. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027 if regulators and El Dorado's owners approve.
DEALS.why: El Dorado brings $2.1 billion of deposits and 35 branches in California and Nevada, taking UMB to 227 branches in 15 states. UMB gets a much bigger West Coast footprint and a cheap, steady base of deposits to fund loans.
DEALS.say: "UMB is paying about $506 million, mostly for El Dorado's $2.1 billion of deposits and 35 West Coast branches, which give it cheap funding and a bigger footprint in California."
q: UMB Financial is paying for El Dorado Savings Bank with about 52% cash and 48% UMB stock. What does the stock part mean for El Dorado's owners?
They must sell their shares back to El Dorado for cash
They become part-owners of UMB and share in its results
They receive UMB bonds that pay a fixed yearly interest rate
They keep their El Dorado shares, which stay publicly listed
Sellers paid in stock swap their shares for the buyer's shares, so they own part of the combined bank and share its future ups and downs.
UMB Financial's ~$506M purchase of El Dorado Savings Bank adds $2.1 billion of deposits and 35 branches. Why do banks often buy other banks for their deposits?
Deposits count as revenue the day the deal closes
Regulators require banks to double deposits every five years
Deposits let a bank skip its own capital requirements
Deposits are a cheap, steady source of money to fund loans
Banks earn money by lending, and customer deposits usually cost much less than borrowing in the bond market, so a big deposit base is valuable.

DEALS.what: French industrial giant Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC, a U.S. maker of design and engineering software, for $205 a share in cash.
DEALS.why: Schneider sells equipment for factories and buildings. Owning PTC's software adds recurring revenue and ties its hardware to the tools engineers use every day.
DEALS.say: "It's a strategic deal: a hardware company paying up for recurring software revenue it can cross-sell to its industrial customers."
q: Schneider is best described as what kind of buyer?
Financial buyer
Strategic buyer
Activist
Sovereign fund
It's an operating company buying a business that fits its own, so it can pay for synergies.
Paying all cash means PTC shareholders:
Become Schneider shareholders
Receive cash and exit
Keep their PTC shares
Get bonds
In an all-cash deal, target shareholders are paid out and no longer own the business.

DEALS.what: Thrive Holdings, a company that buys and runs businesses for the long term, agreed to buy home-security company ADT for $10.00 a share in cash. That values ADT's stock at about $7.6 billion and the whole company, including its debt, at about $15.3 billion.
DEALS.why: ADT will become the base of Thrive's smart-home security business, next to the more than 75 companies it owns in areas like accounting and IT services. Funds managed by Apollo affiliates are providing all of the financing, and the deal has no financing condition.
DEALS.say: "Thrive's $10 cash offer gives ADT a $7.6 billion equity value but a $15.3 billion enterprise value, so roughly half of what Thrive is taking on is ADT's debt and other claims."
q: Thrive Holdings agreed to pay $10.00 cash per ADT share, versus ADT's unaffected close of $6.87. About what premium is that?
($10.00 − $6.87) ÷ $6.87 ≈ 46%; the 52% figure is the premium over ADT's 30-day average price, not its last close.
ADT's deal with Thrive Holdings includes a 30-day go-shop ending Nov 28, 2026. What does that let ADT do?
Sell ADT assets to raise cash before closing
Delay the vote until Apollo's financing is set
Seek rival bids from other buyers for 30 days
Buy back ADT shares at the $10 offer price
A go-shop lets the target actively look for a higher offer after signing, which helps the board show it got the best price.

DEALS.what: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart's parent company, Maplebear, for $65 a share, about $17 billion of equity value. Instacart holders can choose cash, DoorDash stock or a mix, but stock is capped at 25% of the total, and the deal should close by late 2027 or the first half of 2028.
DEALS.why: DoorDash gets the leading U.S. grocery-delivery platform and its retailer software, plus a bigger ad business. Together they can offer local grocers one delivery network to compete with Walmart and Amazon.
DEALS.say: "It's a mostly-cash strategic deal funded with a bridge loan, so the key risks are antitrust review and how much new debt DoorDash takes on while trying to keep its investment-grade rating."
q: DoorDash is paying for Instacart with at least 75% cash and at most 25% DoorDash stock. What is the main benefit of the stock portion for DoorDash?
It uses less new debt and protects the credit rating
It guarantees antitrust approval from regulators
It lets DoorDash skip the shareholder vote
It locks in a lower price per Instacart share
Paying part of the price in stock means borrowing less, which helps DoorDash keep its investment-grade rating.
JPMorgan gave DoorDash a 364-day bridge loan commitment for the Instacart deal. What is a bridge loan used for?
Paying Instacart's employee retention bonuses
Covering the breakup fee if the deal fails
Short-term funding until bonds are issued later
Buying back DoorDash shares after closing
A bridge loan guarantees the cash is there at signing; the buyer usually replaces it with longer-term bonds before or at closing.

DEALS.what: GE Vernova agreed to buy Trench Group, a Berlin-based maker of high-voltage grid parts, from private equity firm Triton Partners for about $9 billion. GE Vernova will pay with roughly equal parts cash and debt, and expects the deal to close in late 2027 after regulatory approvals.
DEALS.why: Trench already supplies GE Vernova, so buying it locks in parts that are in short supply as utilities and data centers rush to expand the power grid. Trench brings about $5 billion of backlog and roughly 33-36% EBITDA margins, which should lift GE Vernova's margins.
DEALS.say: "It's a vertical deal: GE Vernova is buying a key supplier at about 13x forward EBITDA to secure grid capacity, and it hands seller Triton a clean exit to a strategic buyer."
q: GE Vernova is buying Trench Group, a company that already supplies it with grid parts. What kind of acquisition is GE Vernova's Trench deal?
A horizontal deal that removes a direct rival
A conglomerate deal into an unrelated industry
A vertical deal that buys a key supplier
A reverse merger that takes Trench public
Buying a company earlier in your own supply chain is vertical integration, which secures supply and captures the supplier's margin.
GE Vernova values Trench at about 13x its 2028 adjusted EBITDA. Why would a buyer quote a multiple on a future year's EBITDA?
Future EBITDA numbers are always audited by the SEC
Fast growth makes a forward multiple look cheaper
Tax law requires deal prices to use forward figures
Triton insisted on using last year's actual results
For a fast-growing target, a forward-year multiple is lower than a trailing one, so it makes the price look more reasonable.

DEALS.what: Private equity firm EQT agreed to take diagnostics company Qiagen private for €46.50 a share in cash. Including about $1.1 billion of debt, the deal is worth about €10.8 billion (~$12.1 billion).
DEALS.why: Qiagen says private ownership will let it invest for the long term and move faster. Analysts at William Blair put the price at about 15x expected 2027 EBITDA, below similar life-science deals.
DEALS.say: "This is a take-private: EQT pays a ~40% premium over the undisturbed price, measured before takeover rumors leaked in July."
q: The ~40% premium is measured against Qiagen's price before takeover reports in July. Why use that date?
It was the highest price of the year
It is the undisturbed price, before rumors pushed the stock up
Regulators require July prices
It is the date the deal closes
Rumors lift a stock, so premiums are measured from the undisturbed price.
EQT pays €46.50 a share, about a 40% premium. Qiagen's undisturbed share price was roughly:

DEALS.what: Ares Capital (ARCC), the largest business development company (BDC), agreed to buy Apollo-managed lender MidCap Financial (MFIC) in a deal worth about $2.6 billion. MFIC holders get about $10.88 a share, mostly in ARCC stock plus some cash paid by Ares Management, with closing expected in the first half of 2027.
DEALS.why: BDCs are public funds that lend to mid-sized, often PE-owned companies, and scale lowers their costs and borrowing rates. ARCC adds more than 200 loans and says the deal should modestly lift core earnings per share.
DEALS.say: "MFIC traded below its net asset value, so Ares can pay a 30% premium to the share price and still buy the loan book for less than the roughly $12.86 per share it is carried at."
q: Ares Capital is paying MFIC holders about $10.88 a share, mostly in ARCC stock. What does a mostly-stock offer mean for MFIC holders?
They lock in a fixed cash amount at closing
They share in ARCC's future share price moves
They must pay tax at signing, not closing
They lose all ownership in the combined lender
Taking stock means MFIC holders become ARCC owners, so their final value rises or falls with ARCC's shares.
Ares Capital's $10.88 offer is a 30% premium to MFIC's price but below MFIC's ~$12.86 net asset value. Why can both be true?
MFIC's NAV was restated lower by Ares at signing
The premium is measured against the 30-day VWAP
MFIC stock traded at a big discount to its NAV
The cash part is excluded from the premium math
BDC shares often trade below the value of their loans, so a buyer can pay a premium to price and still pay under NAV.

DEALS.what: EQT Corp., the largest U.S. natural gas producer, agreed to buy rival Range Resources by swapping its own shares for Range's. Reuters put Range's equity value at about $12.8 billion, and the combined company is worth more than $50 billion including debt.
DEALS.why: Data centers are driving up demand for natural gas, and a bigger producer can drill more cheaply and sell gas more effectively. EQT expects about $325 million a year in savings within two years, rising to over $600 million long term.
DEALS.say: "It's an all-stock merger of equals in spirit: Range holders take a ~20% premium in EQT shares and end up owning about 27% of the combined gas giant."
q: Range holders get 0.987 EQT shares each. If EQT stock falls 10% before closing, what happens to the value Range holders receive?
It stays fixed at $54.91
It falls too, because the share ratio is fixed
It rises
The deal is cancelled automatically
With a fixed exchange ratio, the target's payout moves with the buyer's stock price.
Why might EQT's stock fall when the deal is announced while Range's jumps?
EQT is paying a premium and issuing new shares, diluting its holders
Range is paying EQT
All-stock deals are illegal
EQT is going private
The buyer pays a premium and issues shares, so its stock often dips while the target rises toward the offer.

DEALS.what: Real estate data company CoStar agreed to buy Vexcel, which flies planes with its own UltraCam cameras to take high-detail aerial photos of 320 big cities and turns them into property data. Vexcel had over $140 million in revenue in the last twelve months, up more than 30%.
DEALS.why: CoStar wants fresher, more accurate property data for its listings and analytics, and plans to use its large sales team to sell Vexcel's data to more customers like insurers. CoStar says the deal should add to its adjusted earnings per share in the first full year.
DEALS.say: "CoStar is paying roughly 5x revenue for Vexcel, a fast-growing data business with mostly recurring contracts, and expects the deal to be accretive in year one."
q: CoStar is paying about $730M for Vexcel, which has about $140M of trailing revenue. Roughly what EV/Revenue multiple is that?
About 2x trailing revenue
About 5x trailing revenue
About 9x trailing revenue
About 14x trailing revenue
$730M divided by about $140M of revenue is roughly 5.2x, an EV/Revenue multiple.
CoStar says buying Vexcel will be accretive to adjusted EPS in year one. What does accretive mean?
CoStar's EPS goes up because of the deal
CoStar's share count goes down after closing
Vexcel's revenue grows faster than CoStar's
CoStar's debt falls because Vexcel pays cash
An accretive deal raises the buyer's earnings per share; a dilutive one lowers it.

terms: Part paid only if milestones are hit
DEALS.what: Swiss drugmaker Ferring, a big name in fertility treatments, signed a deal to buy Gameto, a private biotech that uses cell engineering to develop treatments for infertility and other women's reproductive health issues. The deal is worth up to about $1.38 billion, but part of that is only paid if Gameto hits development, regulatory and sales goals.
DEALS.why: Ferring gets a pipeline of new fertility technology, including an egg-maturation program that is still investigational in the U.S., and can use its global sales network to reach more patients. Tying much of the price to milestones protects Ferring if the science or FDA approval doesn't pan out.
DEALS.say: "Ferring's up-to-$1.38 billion deal for Gameto ties part of the price to future milestones, which is how buyers handle the risk that an unapproved biotech product never makes it to market."
q: Ferring's deal for Gameto is worth 'up to' $1.38B because some payments depend on future milestones. What is that kind of payment called?
Contingent consideration paid later if goals are met
A breakup fee paid if the deal fails to close
A tender offer made directly to public shareholders
A dividend recap funded by new debt at the target
Milestone payments are contingent consideration: the buyer pays more only if the target reaches set goals.
Gameto's main program is not yet FDA approved. Why does that make milestone payments attractive to Ferring when buying Gameto?
They let Ferring avoid any regulatory review of the deal
They make Gameto's shareholders pay Ferring's legal fees
They cut what Ferring pays if the product never gets approved
They guarantee Ferring a fixed return on the whole purchase
Paying part of the price only on success shifts the risk of a failed trial or rejection back to the sellers.

terms: Paid with committed financing and existing resources
DEALS.what: Ahold Delhaize, the Dutch owner of Food Lion, Stop & Shop and Albert, agreed to buy Tesco's grocery business in Czechia and Slovakia for an enterprise value of about €1.2 billion. The unit has more than 360 company-run stores plus 100+ franchise stores and about €3.5 billion in sales.
DEALS.why: Combined with its Albert stores, Ahold expects to become the top grocery brand in Czechia and gains a first foothold in Slovakia. Grocery is a scale game, so more stores mean better buying power with suppliers and lower costs per store.
DEALS.say: "Ahold Delhaize is paying about 7.2 times EBITDA for Tesco's Czech and Slovak stores, but closer to 5 times once you count synergies, which is how a buyer can justify a price that looks higher than it feels."
q: Ahold Delhaize says its Tesco Czechia and Slovakia purchase costs about 7.2x EBITDA, or 5.0x 'including synergies.' Why is the second multiple lower?
Synergies are added to EBITDA, making the denominator larger
Synergies cut the purchase price Ahold Delhaize pays Tesco at closing
The lower multiple leaves out the leases that Tesco's stores carry
The lower multiple uses Tesco's sales instead of EBITDA as its base
Adding expected cost savings to the target's EBITDA makes the denominator bigger, so the price looks cheaper as a multiple.
Ahold Delhaize gives Tesco Czechia and Slovakia two values: ~€1.2B EV and ~€1.7B 'lease-adjusted' EV. What explains the gap?
The €0.5B gap is a breakup fee owed if regulators block the deal
The €0.5B gap is the extra amount Ahold expects to save each year
The €0.5B gap counts store lease obligations as a form of debt
The €0.5B gap is the value of Tesco's franchise stores in Slovakia
Under IFRS 16, store leases are treated like debt, so adding them raises enterprise value; the matching EBITDA is also measured before rent.

DEALS.what: Affle, an Indian mobile ad-tech company, agreed to buy Nasdaq-listed Perion for $11.70 per share in cash, valuing Perion's equity at about $420 million. Perion's board backed the deal, which still needs shareholder and U.S. antitrust approval.
DEALS.why: Affle adds Perion's retail media, connected-TV and digital billboard ad tools to its mobile marketing platform, hoping to sell more to the same advertisers. Perion keeps its brand, and its shareholders get a certain cash price.
DEALS.say: "Affle's all-cash offer for Perion pays a 34.5% premium and includes a 40-day go-shop, which lets Perion's board test the market for a better bid before the deal closes."
src: Perion press release via Yahoo Finance
q: Affle's deal to buy Perion includes a 40-day 'go-shop' period. What does that allow Perion to do?
Ask Affle to raise its $11.70 price once each week
Actively seek competing offers from other buyers
Let Perion holders swap shares for Affle stock
Delay its shareholder vote until regulators approve
A go-shop lets the target solicit rival bids for a set time after signing, helping the board show it got the best price.
Affle is paying $11.70 per share for Perion, a 34.5% premium to its Oct 30 close. Roughly where did Perion stock close that day?
About $8.70, or $11.70 divided by 1.345
About $7.66, or $11.70 minus 34.5% of it
About $15.74, or $11.70 times 1.345
Premium = offer / prior price - 1, so the prior price is $11.70 / 1.345, about $8.70.
